title.es: Recibir a un visitante de intercambio

es: Resolver un fin de semana con un visitante de intercambio: planear, reportar un mensaje, solucionar un imprevisto y hablar de costumbres.

teaching.en: Our exchange student arrives on Friday, so we're planning a busy weekend.
teaching.es: Nuestro estudiante de intercambio llega el viernes, así que estamos planeando un fin de semana ajetreado.
teaching.explanationEs: Para planes ya organizados se usa el presente continuo: we're planning.
segments: Our exchange student arrives on Friday,
so we're planning a busy weekend.
teaching.audioText: Our exchange student arrives on Friday, so we're planning a busy weekend.

teaching.en: The airline told us that the suitcase would be delivered to the house by noon.
teaching.es: La aerolínea nos dijo que la maleta sería entregada en casa antes del mediodía.
teaching.explanationEs: Reporte: told us that + would be delivered; will retrocede a would al reportar.
segments: The airline told us that the suitcase would
be delivered to the house by noon.
teaching.audioText: The airline told us that the suitcase would be delivered to the house by noon.

teaching.en: Take your time to unpack; we can have dinner later if you're tired.
teaching.es: Tómate tu tiempo para deshacer la maleta; podemos cenar más tarde si estás cansado.
teaching.explanationEs: Una oferta amable: can + verbo base, y if + presente para la condición.
segments: Take your time to unpack; we can
have dinner later if you're tired.
teaching.audioText: Take your time to unpack; we can have dinner later if you're tired.

teaching.en: In our house, it's a custom to eat together at eight, and you'll soon get used to it.
teaching.es: En nuestra casa es costumbre comer juntos a las ocho, y pronto te acostumbrarás.
teaching.explanationEs: It's a custom to + verbo; get used to + pronombre o -ing para la adaptación.
segments: In our house, it's a custom to eat together
at eight, and you'll soon get used to it.
teaching.audioText: In our house, it's a custom to eat together at eight, and you'll soon get used to it.

teaching.en: He must have been exhausted after such a long flight.
teaching.es: Debió de quedar agotado después de un vuelo tan largo.
teaching.explanationEs: Must have + participio es una deducción sobre el pasado.
teaching.audioText: He must have been exhausted after such a long flight.

teaching.en: The restaurant had no free table, so we had pizza delivered instead.
teaching.es: El restaurante no tenía mesa libre, así que pedimos pizza a domicilio.
teaching.explanationEs: Have + cosa + participio: alguien hace el servicio por ti; aquí, traer la pizza.
segments: The restaurant had no free table,
so we had pizza delivered instead.
teaching.audioText: The restaurant had no free table, so we had pizza delivered instead.

choices.text: Tom said me that his flight was delayed.
Tom told me that his flight would be delayed.
Tom told me that his flight was delayed.

feedback.es: Se reporta con told + persona + that, y el presente is pasa a was. Said me lleva mal la persona, y would be delayed cambia el mensaje a un futuro que Tom no dijo.

hint.es: Reporta con told + persona + that y retrocede el tiempo.

feedback.es: Have + cosa + participio: nosotros encargamos que la pizza llegue a casa.

origin.text: We had pizza ___ to the house.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Te acostumbrarás pronto a cenar tarde.»

answer.text: You will soon get used to eating late
accepted: You will soon get used to eating late
You will get used to eating late soon
Soon you will get used to eating late
You'll soon get used to eating late

feedback.es: Get used to lleva -ing porque to es una preposición.

hint.es: Después de get used to va un verbo con -ing.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la función que cumple en la visita.

pairs: Do you mean the train or the bus?

pairs.es: aclarar lo que dijo otra persona

pairs: It's a custom to eat together.
We're going to the market on Saturday.

feedback.es: Cada frase resuelve una necesidad: aclarar, solucionar, hablar de costumbres y planear.

pairs: Do you mean the train or the bus?

pairs.es: aclarar lo que dijo otra persona

pairs: It's a custom to eat together.
We're going to the market on Saturday.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le dijo la familia anfitriona.

choices.text: They said the meal would start at eight o'clock.
They said the meal had started at eight.
They said the meal would be at six.

feedback.es: La familia dijo que la cena sería a las ocho: would reporta el futuro de la cena desde el pasado. Had started diría que ya empezó, y las seis es otra hora.

origin.audio: The host family told me that dinner would be at eight, so I have time to shower first.

prompt.es: Explica a tu visitante una costumbre de tu casa.

answer.text: In our house, it's a custom to take off your shoes at the door.
accepted: In our house, it's a custom to take off your shoes at the door.
It is a custom in our house to take off your shoes at the door.
In my house, it's a custom to take off your shoes when you come in.
In our house it's a custom to take off our shoes at the door.

feedback.es: Se usa it's a custom to + verbo. Sin it, la oración queda incompleta; la rúbrica pide la costumbre, los zapatos y la puerta.

origin.text: En tu casa todos se quitan los zapatos en la puerta y quieres que tu visitante lo sepa.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige de qué depende el plan del domingo.

choices.text: It depends on how Tom feels.
It depends on the train times.

feedback.es: La frase if Tom isn't too tired condiciona el plan de ir a la playa: depende de cómo se sienta Tom, no del tiempo.

origin.audio: We're visiting the market on Saturday, and on Sunday we're going to the beach if Tom isn't too tired.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es el reporte correcto de lo que dijo Tom?

choices.text: Tom told Ana to wait for him.
Tom told Ana don't wait for him.
Tom told Ana not to wait for him.

feedback.es: Tell + persona + not to + verbo reporta una petición negativa. To wait cambia el sentido a afirmativo, y don't no se usa en el estilo indirecto.

origin.text: Tom: "Please don't wait for me, Ana."

prompt.es: Completa: «Debió de estar agotado después de tantas horas de vuelo.»

feedback.es: Must have + participio expresa una deducción sobre algo pasado.

origin.text: He must ___ been exhausted after so many hours in the air.

prompt.es: Escribe tu resumen del fin de semana con los datos dados, de 50 a 110 palabras.

answer.text: Tom arrived on Friday, and this weekend we're visiting the market on Saturday and going to the beach on Sunday. The airline told us that his suitcase would be delivered on Sunday. The restaurant was full on Friday, so we had dinner delivered to the house. In our house, it's a custom to eat together at nine, and Tom is getting used to it. I hope he will enjoy the weekend.
accepted: Tom arrived on Friday, and this weekend we're visiting the market on Saturday and going to the beach on Sunday. The airline told us that his suitcase would be delivered on Sunday. The restaurant was full on Friday, so we had dinner delivered to the house. In our house, it's a custom to eat together at nine, and Tom is getting used to it. I hope he will enjoy the weekend.

Tom arrived on Friday. On Saturday we are visiting the market, and on Sunday we will go to the beach. The airline said that his suitcase would arrive on Sunday. The restaurant was full on Friday, so we had food delivered to the house. It is a custom in our house to eat together at nine, and Tom is getting used to it. I hope he will enjoy the weekend.

feedback.es: El resumen cubre el plan, el mensaje reportado, el imprevisto resuelto con have + participio y una costumbre.

origin.text: Datos: Tom llegó el viernes. Plan: el sábado visitáis el mercado y el domingo vais a la playa. Mensaje: la aerolínea os dijo que su maleta sería entregada el domingo. Imprevisto: el viernes el restaurante estaba lleno y pedisteis la cena a domicilio. Costumbre: en tu casa se cena juntos a las nueve y Tom se está acostumbrando.

evidenceGroups: we will go to the market
we are going to the market

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase sirve para aclarar lo que dijo el visitante?

choices.text: Do you mean you don't like fish?
You don't like fish, so you will eat it.
I think you don't like fish.

feedback.es: Do you mean…? pide confirmar el significado sin suponerlo. Las otras dos dan por hecho lo que quiso decir.

origin.text: Tom mira el pescado de su plato y dice: "I can't eat that."

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se está acostumbrando a desayunar con nosotros.»

answer.text: He is getting used to having breakfast with us

feedback.es: Get used to lleva -ing; is getting indica que la adaptación está en proceso.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué lamenta el visitante.

feedback.es: I wish I had brought lamenta algo del pasado: no haber traído ropa más abrigada.

origin.audio: I wish I had brought warmer clothes; it's much colder here than I expected.
